correctness.rationale: On all labelled connected simple graphs for n>=1, partition-lattice Möbius inversion gives W(S)=sum_{pi:E(pi)∩S=empty}(-1)^(k-1)(k-1)! 2^e(pi). Boolean-lattice zeta inversion is unimodular, so the integer ideal generated by all W(S) equals that generated by all partition weights. The lower bound e(pi)>=n-k and Legendre's valuation of (k-1)! imply exponent >=n-1-floor(log2 n). Taking k=2^L blocks composed of t=n-2^L doubletons and the remaining singletons attains this exponent; a two-block partition gives a pure power-of-two weight so no odd prime divides the gcd (n=1 weight 1). Inverse zeta on matching subsets forces a sharp witness among j<=t positive-sign matching edges and yields the displayed exact finite factorial sum. An independently coded graph-connectivity enumerator/Walsh butterfly checked complete integer spectra n=1..5 and gcds 1,1,2,2,4. The finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: Connectivity on the binary complete-edge space is a canonical graph-theoretic Boolean function.
